terms.grammar: frequēns, “often present”, agreeing with the subject
terms.comment: Traupman’s phrase. Each word is classical (frequēns of a person who is often present), but the phrase is not in Lewis & Short or the loci collections.

evidence: Sen. Ep. 32.1: ubi et cum quibus morēris (Lewis & Short)

sources: Lewis & Short: moror
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 100, checked against the searchable text and the page image (12 November 2026).: p. 325.
